messages:
maya: Quick sync — dedupe signals vs tenant fanout. We keep seeing duplicate spans/metrics from client retries and mobile reconnects. Two high-level options: 1) do a best-effort dedupe at the ingest edge (fast, lossy) and fanout only unique-ish ids; 2) always fanout everything to tenant shards and dedupe downstream with canonical storage. Want tradeoffs and gotchas.

jonathan: What are our main constraints? latency vs cost vs correctness?

maya: All three. Product wants low tail-latency for dashboards, infra wants to avoid N× fanout cost when a client spikes, and platform wants correctness for billing attribution (no double-charge).

sara: Biggest risk with edge dedupe is false negatives — different clients might compute slightly different signatures and we drop legit events. Also need to consider cross-region duplicates.

kevin: Proposal sketch: compute a cheap signature at edge: sha1(client_id + trace_id + span_id + floor(ts/10s)). If signature seen in short-lived LRU cache, drop fanout. Otherwise forward. Downstream still stores canonical event id for stronger dedupe during write.

adaline: Hm sequence numbers would be nicer but many SDKs don't provide. Also if we rely on TTL cache at edge we have to dimension properly: how big, per-region vs global?
\ninfra-bot: incident-alert: ingest-queue-backlog > 80% for 3m — note that dedupe strategy needs to play well with backpressure.

kevin: Right — if edge dedupe reduces fanout, it helps backpressure. But if edge dedupe is lossy and we drop enough data to break billing accuracy, that's bad. So hybrid sounds safe: edge-level cheap signature to cut obvious immediate retries + downstream deterministic idempotent writes with a bounded dedupe window (e.g., 5m).

jonathan: Operational complexity: hybrid needs coordination on signature format and cache invalidation. Also testing: we need a replay harness to measure false-positive drop rate.

sara: Cost numbers (very rough): fanout-per-event to 8 tenant shards =~ +0.9ms p95 and +$0.00012/event. If duplicates are 5% of events, that's a decent saving. But if duplicates are bursty (50% during retries) we could save a lot.

maya: What about ordering? If we dedupe at edge, we may change ordering guarantees for downstream consumers that assume arrival order. Is that acceptable?

kevin: We can attach an original-ingest-ts header so consumers can reconstruct ordering for a given trace id. But reordering could still happen during network partitions. Need consumers to be resilient.

adaline: Security/abuse: signatures based on client-provided ids are subject to collision attacks. We should salt with region and a server secret.

kevin: Example pseudo-code for edge signature:

```
secret = ENV.EDGE_SALT
sig = sha1(secret + "|" + client_id + "|" + trace_id + "|" + span_id + "|" + (ts // 10000))
if edgeCache.has(sig): drop else edgeCache.add(sig, ttl=300s); forward
```

maya: Good. Action items: (1) kevin + adaline run a small perf sim to estimate cache size and FP rate (due next Wed); (2) jonathan + sara build replay harness against current prod traces to measure duplicate signature match rate; (3) i'll draft an RFC describing hybrid approach and schema for signature and headers.

jonathan: Agree. Also include rollback plan: a feature flag at ingress to toggle dedupe and a metric (#dropped_by_edge) we can monitor.

sara: +1 on metrics. Add a billing-sanity check that runs daily comparing invoiceable-unique-events pre/post dedupe rollout.

maya: I'll own the RFC. Assigning owners: @kevin (edge impl), @adaline (simulation), @jonathan (harness), @sara (billing checks). I'll post a link to the draft in #eng-platform when ready. :thumbsup:

kevin: :eyes: starting sim today.

adaline: Will look at per-region cache sharding options.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: created feature-flag "ingest_edge_dedupe" in staging.

maya: Thanks everyone — short sync done.
